newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips profit slumps, major one-off cost to come.
newsitem.headline: Philips profit slumps, major one-off cost to come.

text.p: Dutch electronics giant Philips Electronics NV on Thursday reported a slump in third-quarter profits and warned of a one billion guilder ($580 million) extraordinary charge in the current final quarter.
Philips shares plunged 3.20 guilders or more than five percent to 53.40 after the shock news, which was much worse than market analysts had expected.
Third-quarter net profit from normal operations dropped to 123 million guilders from 539 million a year ago. Analysts had expected earnings of between 240 and 360 million guilders.

Some in the market had expected Philips to take a third-quarter charge to cover ongoing restructuring within the group but the group's new president, Cor Boonstra, instead gave advance warning of a one billion guilder extraordinary charge in the fourth quarter.

"Analysis of our business...demonstrates the need to accelerate planned actions for recovery. Consequently we anticipate that we will recognise a charge in the fourth quarter of 1996 of approximately one billion guilders before tax," he said in a statement.
Philips said its third-quarter business performance was "most disappointing".
"The anticipated recovery of sales and income has not materialised," it said in a statement. ($1=1.710 Guilder)
